learningObjective: Identify All-to-All as the collective that permutes per-rank shards and its canonical role in MoE dispatch.

canonicalClaims.claim: All-to-All is a data-permutation collective in which each rank sends a distinct 1/N-shard to every other rank and receives a distinct 1/N-shard from every other rank, and it is the standard primitive for dispatching / combining tokens across experts in expert-parallel MoE.
conditions: The input tensor on each rank is logically partitioned into N shards, one per destination rank.
The volume moved per rank is (N-1)/N · S bytes over the fabric (self-shard stays local).
nonImplications: Does not imply any arithmetic reduction is applied to the payloads.
Does not imply that All-to-All is the cheapest way to redistribute all data; when the whole tensor is needed on every rank, AllGather is preferred.

sourceMappings.locator: § discussion of All-to-All patterns for expert parallelism

misconceptions.claim: All-to-All is a broadcast: every rank sends its entire tensor to every other rank and receives a copy of every peer's tensor.
misconceptions.whyWrong: That is AllGather (with N-way replication). All-to-All sends and receives distinct 1/N-shards, so no rank ends with N-fold data.

misconceptions.claim: All-to-All performs a summation of per-rank shards, analogous to AllReduce along one axis.
misconceptions.whyWrong: All-to-All is pure data movement with no reduction; it only permutes shards across ranks.

misconceptions.claim: All-to-All is unnecessary in expert-parallel MoE because AllReduce over expert outputs achieves the same routing.
misconceptions.whyWrong: MoE routing needs to send each token to the specific expert that owns it and later return it to the origin rank; this is a permutation, not a reduction. AllReduce would destroy per-token identity.
